pr_body:
Adds some additional functionality to read rows. 
- allows missing entries in schema, closes #2634 
- adds a 'schema' parameter for specifying own schema. (this will coerce any values that do not match given schema).
- adds `inferSchemaLength` for reading from rows. 

Also adds `unique_stable`

@ritchie46 I managed to get a generic `infer_schema` working, and I moved that logic into `frame/row`. The row reader for py & rust still uses the current implementation. I didn't want this to be a big refactor, but I could submit a followup PR to have py & rust use the same logic.

issue_context.title: Allow missing entries when reading from rows
issue_context.body:
I assume this is considered a feature request. In `nodejs-polars`, I want to _tabulate_ a javascript an array-nesting-objects into a _polars_ dataframe.
It's a straightforward task _if_ we have a _consistent_ structure with all properties existing in all objects:
```javascript
const myData = [
    {
        "id": "a",
        "name": "fred",
        "country": "france",
        "age": 30
    },
    {
        "id": "b",
        "name": "alexandra",
        "country": "usa",
        "age": 40
    },
    {
        "id": "c",
        "name": "george",
        "country": "argentina",
        "age": 50
    }
]
```
So we can do:
```javascript
const pl = require("nodejs-polars")

const output = pl.DataFrame(myData)
```
And we get a _polars_ dataframe as expected.

**However,** a slight inconsistency in the properties (across objects) causes it to fail:
```javascript
const myDataInconsistent = [
    {
        "id": "a",
        "name": "fred",
        "country": "france",
        "age": 30,
        "city": "paris" // there's no "city" property elsewhere
    },
    {
        "id": "b",
        "name": "alexandra",
        "country": "usa",
        "age": 40
    },
    {
        "id": "c",
        "name": "george",
        "country": "argentina",
        "age": 50
    }
]

const output = pl.DataFrame(myData)
``` 
> Error: Lengths don't match: Could not create a new DataFrame from Series. The Series have different lengths

---
Ideally, I would expect that properties that don't exist for some records but do appear in others, will either be populated with the value or become `null` in the dataframe.

---
[Originally I posted this as a question on Stack Overflow.](https://stackoverflow.com/q/71100864/6105259)
comments: Thanks for the question. @universalmind303 can likely help you on this one.

@ritchie46 the same behavior is present in python. 

```py
import polars as pl

rows_first = [
    {"foo": 1, "bar": "a"},
    {"foo": 0}
]

rows_last = [
    {"foo": 1},
    {"foo": 0, "bar": "a"}
]

df1 = pl.DataFrame(rows_first, orient="row")  # errors
df2 = pl.DataFrame(rows_last, orient="row")  # works, but column 'bar' is missing
```

I actually was thinking about this when I was implementing the row oriented reader for JS. 
Adding an `infer_schema_length`, or `schema` argument for reading from row oriented dicts seems like it would fix the problem.  

Another approach would be to implement ser/de for rows.

> Originally I posted this as a question on Stack Overflow.

I didn't realize there was a SO tag for nodejs-polars. I just subscribed to it to make sure im informed on future SO questions.

@emmansh I should have a fix for this soon, still working out some kinks & testing.  

not only will it be easier to read from rows, It will also be faster.
